origins.section: A Fail-Fast Iterator Checks a Counter on Every Step, and One Thread Is Enough to Trip It
The Check Is Best-Effort: Some Changes Slip Past It
A CopyOnWriteArrayList Iterator Walks the Array It Started With
A ConcurrentHashMap Walk Never Throws, and It Is Not a Snapshot

recorded.prompt:q-bundle-keys:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-bundle-keys:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-bundle-keys:c: The page states 'Replacing the value of an existing key isn't structural, so it isn't counted' and its output shows put(existing key) completing.
recorded.prompt:q-bundle-keys:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-bundle-keys:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-bundle-keys:d: The page says next() throws once the counters differ and shows put(new key) producing ConcurrentModificationException, so the walk does not carry on.
recorded.prompt:q-five-refunds:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-five-refunds:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-five-refunds:b: The page says 'A walk that ends without an exception proves nothing' and its example shows j4 never visited.

recorded.pass:q-five-refunds:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-five-refunds:c: The page shows the check trips on a same-thread change ('No second thread is involved') and that here the loop ended before next() could check.

recorded.pass:q-five-refunds:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-five-refunds:d: The page says an ArrayList iterator holds an index into the list and a removal shifts later elements down, so it walks the live list; walking the starting array is the CopyOnWriteArrayList behavior.
